facts.text: Mill Creek earned its name from a nearby stream once called Spring Run, where an early sawmill sparked settlement and a post office opened in 1876 near a railroad crossing on the Kankakee River.
European settlers first arrived in 1831 when Horace and Lane Markham built cabins beside a local stream, later renamed Mill Creek for its milling potential.
The community sits inside the Kankakee River watershed, part of the Mississippi River basin, where glacial meltwater history shapes current surface water patterns.
What is now productive farmland was once a vast freshwater marsh; today, the area balances agriculture with ongoing wetland preservation efforts.
Before European arrival, the Potawatomi, Ottawa, and Sac tribes used the Mill Creek area for seasonal hunting, fishing, and gathering along its prairies and waterways.
